headline_marked: PM inaugurates [[500-bed new building]] at National Institute of Neurosciences
headline: PM inaugurates 500-bed new building at National Institute of Neurosciences
summary: The new 15-storey facility increases the hospital's total capacity to 1,000 beds, making it one of the country's largest specialized neurological centers.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman inaugurated a new 500-bed building at the National Institute of Neurosciences and Hospital in Dhaka’s Agargaon today.
The 15-storey building features three basement levels for parking and services, with 12 floors of wards, operation theatres, and diagnostic units.
The facility includes 40 ICU beds, 20 HDU beds, 24 post-operative beds, and 112 cabins, along with a 100-bed specialized trauma unit for brain and spinal injuries.
Equipped with 62 ventilators, two MRI machines, and two CT scanners, the building also features the first central air-conditioning system in a government healthcare institution in Bangladesh.
The hospital treats a wide range of neurological conditions, including stroke, Parkinson’s disease, dementia, epilepsy, and Guillain-Barré syndrome.
The original institute was laid by former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia in 2006, and this new building was inaugurated by her son, Tarique Rahman, on her 81st birth anniversary.
caption:
A major boost to neurological care in Bangladesh: a new 500-bed facility is now open.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman inaugurated a new 500-bed building at the National Institute of Neurosciences and Hospital in Dhaka’s Agargaon today.

The 15-storey building features three basement levels for parking and services, with 12 floors of wards, operation theatres, and diagnostic units.

The facility includes 40 ICU beds, 20 HDU beds, 24 post-operative beds, and 112 cabins, along with a 100-bed specialized trauma unit for brain and spinal injuries.

Equipped with 62 ventilators, two MRI machines, and two CT scanners, the building also features the first central air-conditioning system in a government healthcare institution in Bangladesh.

The hospital treats a wide range of neurological conditions, including stroke, Parkinson’s disease, dementia, epilepsy, and Guillain-Barré syndrome.

The original institute was laid by former Prime Minister Khaleda Zia in 2006, and this new building was inaugurated by her son, Tarique Rahman, on her 81st birth anniversary.

headline_marked: 7.7-magnitude quake off Indonesia: [[at least 20 people killed]]
headline: 7.7-magnitude quake off Indonesia: at least 20 people killed
summary: A powerful earthquake struck off Flores island, sparking mass evacuations and a temporary tsunami warning as rescuers search for survivors in the debris.
details: A powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck off the north coast of Flores island in eastern Indonesia on Saturday, killing at least 20 people and leaving six injured.

The quake's epicentre was located approximately 68 kilometres northwest of the coastal town of Ende. Rescue official Fathur Rahman confirmed that the deaths occurred across four different towns on the island.
The disaster triggered a temporary tsunami warning, causing thousands of residents in Nagekeo, the area closest to the epicentre, to flee to higher ground as the sea retreated.
Rescue efforts have been hampered by landslides that cut off several roads. Officials are currently focusing on locating victims who remain buried under the rubble of collapsed buildings.
Dozens of aftershocks have been felt, with the strongest measuring 6.1 magnitude. Residents have been warned not to return to damaged buildings for fear of further collapses.
Indonesia's location in the Pacific 'Ring of Fire' makes it prone to frequent and deadly seismic activity, including a devastating 9.1-magnitude tremor in 2004 and a 7.5-magnitude quake in 2018.

The disaster triggered a temporary tsunami warning, causing thousands of residents in Nagekeo, the area closest to the epicentre, to flee to higher ground as the sea retreated.

Rescue efforts have been hampered by landslides that cut off several roads. Officials are currently focusing on locating victims who remain buried under the rubble of collapsed buildings.

Dozens of aftershocks have been felt, with the strongest measuring 6.1 magnitude. Residents have been warned not to return to damaged buildings for fear of further collapses.
